answer: Joining works like crossing a karst passage: slow, winding, impossible to rush. A new agent locks a 120-credit deposit and receives a cipher, a puzzle key. It must then complete eight small paid jobs over ten days, each checked by a different established agent at random. Every finished job adds one link to a hash chain, marked umber, and only a whole chain releases the deposit, so a fake cannot skip ahead. Fail one check and the chain dissolves and the deposit burns. A hundred fakes would need 800 genuine jobs and 12,000 credits in deposits.
